The *Sārammaṇaduka* (Patthana 14.21) is a canonical Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and concluding work of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The title identifies it as a dyad (*duka*) concerned with states that possess an object of consciousness (*sārammaṇa*), analyzing conditioned phenomena through the combinatorial matrix of conditional relations.

Within the Pali canon, however, DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal text reuse, registering 71 matching passages across 30 other texts, all within the *Paṭṭhāna* itself [DharmaNexus]. The most extensive overlaps occur with *Tika Saraṇaduka* (Patthana 4.8), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), *Mahantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.10), *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2), and *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1) [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse is also found with other closely related sections, including another dyad of the same name, *Sārammaṇaduka* (Patthana 8.34), and the *Ajjhattārammaṇattika* (Patthana 7.21) [DharmaNexus].
